title: Dashboard Aggregate
description: The cross-assignment roll-up at reports/dashboard.json, and the only file the org overview reads. THREE surfaces write it and until this schema existed none of them validated it: report/report.mjs rebuilds one entry and prunes the dead ones, AdminView's syncDashboardState merge-patches the fields an assignment document owns, and AssignmentDetailView's syncDashboardAggregate rebuilds one entry from a synthesised assignment. The e2e fixture validates every other control-repo write and had to skip this path for want of a schema, so a malformed dashboard was the one document no test could catch. Entries are built by lib/dashboard-aggregate.mjs and nothing else; tests/dashboard-schema.test.mjs derives this property list from that builder's real output rather than keeping a second copy of it.

assignments.description: One entry per assignment that has been reported on, keyed by assignment id. An assignment created but never reported on is absent, which is why the dashboard reads assignments/ as well.

propertyNames.description: The assignment id, spelled exactly as assignment.schema.json constrains it.

generated_at.description: When the file was last rewritten by a full regeneration (report.mjs) or a live refresh. NOT set by the two patch paths - closing an assignment and deleting one both rewrite the file and leave this alone - so it is the age of the counts, not of the document. Nothing reads it today; it is declared so the next surface to want it knows which of the two questions it answers.

entry.description: One assignment's card on the overview: the facts the assignment document owns, plus the counts derived from its report.

title.description: Copied from the assignment document, which requires it.

state.description: Optional because assignment.schema.json does not require `state` either, and an entry may not invent one. Its absence used to be invisible: the overview read this file's state and only publish-assignment.yml ever asked for a regeneration, so a closed assignment went on reading 'accepting' until syncDashboardState started patching it (reported 2026-09-04).

deadline_at.description: The class deadline. A student with an override is judged against their own, which lives on the report row, never here.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for display. Optional for the same reason as `state`.

max_acceptances.description: The cap, so a surface holding only this entry can tell 'live' from 'cap reached' without re-reading the assignment YAML. Null means no cap, never a substituted number.

total_students.description: The cohort, not the org roster: an assignment naming class_groups counts only those groups' students.

accepted.description: Report rows whose acceptance_state is not 'not-accepted'. A row exists for every student on the roster, accepted or not, which is why this is a filter and not total_students.

with_repo_faults.description: Rows warning `missing-repo-id`, and only those - the one fault the detail view still shows and the only one a lecturer can act on. Named `with_warnings` before 2026-09-02, when it counted two warnings that had left the detail table and sent lecturers to a page with nothing on it.

generated_at.description: When THIS entry's counts were computed. Per entry because entries are regenerated one at a time: a nightly run for one assignment leaves every other entry, and its timestamp, exactly as it was.
